pathway.title: Wolverine World Wide Inc /De/ — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage has moved from stretched to moderate through both repayment and earnings. Net debt to EBITDA was 4.01x at FY2024, 2.36x at FY2025 and 1.66x at Q3 2026, which is 1.69x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-02, with net debt falling from USD 495.9 million to USD 399.3 million (USD 407.5 million pro forma) while EBITDA rose from USD 123.7 million in FY2024 to USD 241.2 million on an LTM basis. That lowers debt service pressure and the weight of the 2029 maturity, but the ratio is seasonal: it was 2.76x at Q1 2026 after the first-quarter working capital build. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation L3

Part of the latest improvement is one-off, and the underlying margin is flat rather than rising. Tariff refunds of USD 32.6 million sit in cost of goods sold, so gross margin without them was 47.41% in the first nine months of 2026, level with 47.41% a year earlier, which means price increases and other gains only matched higher U.S. tariff costs and an unfavourable product and customer mix. EBITDA margin without the refund was 10.49% against 8.96% a year earlier because operating expenses grew 3.0% while revenue grew 8.3%, so operating leverage added 1.53 percentage points rather than the 3.75 percentage points reported. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation L11; calculation L12; calculation L13

The 2029 senior notes are the single refinancing event, and liquidity covers them with room to spare. Liquidity of USD 724.7 million, which is cash plus USD 576.6 million of unborrowed revolver, is 1.32x the USD 550.0 million principal, no debt matures before 2029-08-15 (about 33 months from the as-of date), and the notes carry an annual cash coupon of USD 22.0 million. The revolver ends 405 days after the notes, so it does not by itself bridge a failed refinancing, and whether it carries an earlier springing maturity is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L6; calculation L7; calculation L8; calculation L16

Free cash flow is positive but seasonal and driven by working capital, not investment. Capital expenditure was only USD 14.5 million in fiscal 2025, so free cash flow was USD 125.5 million, USD 77.7 million after USD 33.3 million of dividends and USD 14.5 million of repurchases, and USD 211.5 million on an LTM basis; nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 20.1 million in 2025 and positive USD 65.9 million in 2026. Revolver borrowings rose to USD 92.0 million at Q1 2026 from USD 75.0 million at the year-end before being repaid, so intra-year leverage and liquidity should be read against the same quarter a year earlier. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation L9; calculation L10; calculation L24

Business concentration is the main operating risk. The Active Group supplied 75.1% of fiscal 2025 revenue and 71.4% of segment profit before corporate costs, led by Saucony and Merrell, while the Work Group's operating margin fell to 14.9% from 16.4% in the first nine months of 2026; brand revenue levels are not printed, so the size of the dependence is not established, and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation L21

Tariffs and Asian sourcing are the main external risk, and no contract protects the margin. All products come from third-party suppliers, mainly in Asia Pacific, without long-term contracts, so U.S. tariff costs flow into cost of goods sold and are recovered only through price; the February 2026 court ruling produced a one-off refund and no further asset is recognised. Footwear is a competitive and fragmented market and wholesale customers order on an order-to-order basis, so the evidence of pricing power is price increases offsetting tariffs rather than margin expansion. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation L11

Claims outside reported debt make obligations larger than the debt figure suggests. Total debt plus the USD 125.0 million of receivables sold is 2.79x LTM EBITDA, USD 137.3 million of lease liabilities and USD 53.0 million of accrued pension liabilities sit outside debt, and the USD 21.4 million environmental reserve will be paid over up to 25 years. Goodwill and intangibles of USD 633.8 million exceed equity of USD 533.9 million, so an impairment would hit equity but not cash. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; calculation L17; calculation L22; calculation L23

Financial policy and governance are moderate, and they hold the main unknowns for creditors. There is no sponsor, payouts are 38.1% of free cash flow and no waiver, exchange or restructuring is described, but the covenant levels, the security and ranking of the notes and the proxy statement are not available, so headroom and priority are not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation L10

cells.text: Designer, marketer and licensor of casual, performance outdoor and athletic, kids', work and uniform footwear and apparel, sold in approximately 170 countries and territories through owned operations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and parts of Europe and Asia Pacific, and through distributors, licensees and joint ventures elsewhere

Active Group: Merrell, Saucony, Sweaty Betty and Chaco. Work Group: Wolverine, Cat, Bates, Harley-Davidson and HYTEST. Other: Hush Puppies, sourcing commissions, a multi-brand store and the Stride Rite licence. Corporate: unallocated costs, reorganization and environmental costs
Fiscal 2025: Active Group 75.1%, Work Group 22.5% and Other 2.4% of USD 1,874.3 million; nine months of 2026: Active Group 78.1%, Work Group 19.6% and Other 2.3% of USD 1,469.4 million
Fiscal 2025: Active Group 71.4%, Work Group 20.5% and Other 8.1% of USD 354.5 million of segment operating profit before USD 204.3 million of corporate costs
Wholesale including royalties 74.6% and direct-to-consumer 25.4% of fiscal 2025 revenue; 128 retail stores and 39 eCommerce sites at 2026-01-03, and 122 stores and 41 sites at 2026-10-03
United States 47.8% and foreign 52.2% of fiscal 2025 revenue; Europe, Middle East and Africa is the largest foreign region at USD 601.5 million
No customer accounts for more than 10% of consolidated revenue in any year; wholesale sales are generally order-to-order and subject to cancellation and rescheduling rights
All footwear, apparel and accessories are sourced from third-party suppliers, primarily in Asia Pacific, with no long-term contracts with manufacturers

Cat licence through 2028-12-31 and Harley-Davidson licence through 2029-12-31, both open to early termination for breach; Stride Rite and Hush Puppies are licensed to third parties; USD 23.8 million of fixed licence consideration remains to December 2029

Moderate sales seasonality; working capital builds near the end of the first and third quarters and operating cash flow is stronger in the second half; working capital is met from operating cash flow and, as needed, the revolver
No owned factories; capital expenditure of USD 14.5 million, 0.8% of revenue, in fiscal 2025
Approximately 3,050 domestic and foreign retail, distribution, office and sales employees at 2026-01-03

runs.text: Deleveraging to a moderate level is the first strength. Repayment and EBITDA growth took net leverage from 4.01x to 1.66x, or 1.69x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-02, which lowers debt service pressure and the weight of the 2029 maturity and so lowers the probability of distress. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation L3

Liquidity against a single maturity is the second strength. Liquidity of USD 724.7 million covers the USD 550.0 million of notes due on 2029-08-15 by 1.32x and no other debt matures first, so a refinancing can be run without a liquidity squeeze if the revolver stays drawable. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation L6; calculation L7; calculation L16

Asset-light cash generation is the third strength. Capital expenditure of 0.8% of revenue means most EBITDA converts to free cash flow, which was USD 125.5 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 211.5 million over the LTM, supporting repayment and the dividend. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation L9; calculation L10

Active Group brand momentum is the fourth strength. Active Group revenue rose USD 161.7 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 112.8 million in nine months of 2026, lifting EBITDA and the pace of repayment. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation L21

Concentration in the Active Group is the first weakness. The Active Group is 75.1% of revenue and 71.4% of segment profit, so a fade in Saucony or Merrell demand would reverse leverage gains quickly, and brand revenue levels are not printed to size the exposure. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation L21

Tariff exposure and a flattered margin are the second weakness. Third-party Asian sourcing exposes cost of goods sold to tariffs, and USD 32.6 million of one-off refunds lift the latest margin, so leverage is 1.91x before the dividend without them and the underlying gross margin is flat. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L4; calculation L11; calculation L12

A single bullet maturity with unseen terms is the third weakness. All refinancing falls on 2029-08-15, a one percentage point higher coupon would cost USD 5.5 million a year, and covenant levels and the ranking of the notes are not available, so headroom and priority are not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation L16; calculation L19

Claims outside debt and intangibles above equity are the fourth weakness. Receivables sold, lease and pension liabilities and the remediation reserve sit outside the debt figure, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 633.8 million exceed equity of USD 533.9 million, so obligations are larger than debt and an impairment would weaken equity. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation L17; calculation L22; calculation L23

Owned headquarters of about 307,000 square feet in Rockford, Michigan; leased distribution centres of about 720,000 square feet in Beaumont, California, 468,000 in Howard City, Michigan, 215,000 in Ontario, Canada and 125,000 in Heerhugowaard, Netherlands; retail stores leased from third parties

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction or new debt issue is described in the five filings for fiscal 2025 or 2026, and no transaction is pending. The portfolio changes in the filings are disposals and licensing in 2023 and 2024: the Keds, Sperry and leather businesses and the Hush Puppies rights in China, Hong Kong and Macau were sold, the Merrell and Saucony China joint ventures were sold to a licensee, and the kids and apparel lines of those two brands were licensed from May 2024, raising USD 307.8 million of cash with two sale-leasebacks. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 108–110; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation K12

The only financing event in the period is the 2025 Replacement Facility of 2025-09-24, which replaced the revolver and the term loan A with a USD 600.0 million revolver maturing 2030-09-24, guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries and secured on substantially all personal and real property, with aggregate debt capacity of up to USD 850.0 million including incremental debt. The USD 550.0 million 4.000% senior notes issued on 2021-08-26 are due 2029-08-15 and guaranteed by substantially all domestic subsidiaries; they are the only debt outstanding at 2026-10-03, when total debt was USD 547.4 million after USD 2.6 million of deferred financing costs. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15

A quarterly dividend of USD 0.10 per share was declared on 2026-11-02 for holders of record on 2027-01-04; it is a subsequent event after the 2026-10-03 balance sheet and is not in any period figure. The filings describe no refinancing plan, new issue or covenant amendment after the balance sheet date. Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation K14

fields.value: Net leverage fell from 4.01x at FY2024 to 2.36x at FY2025, rose to 2.76x at Q1 2026 on the seasonal build in working capital, and then fell to 2.29x at Q2 2026 and 1.66x at Q3 2026. Net debt moved from USD 495.9 million at FY2024 to USD 399.3 million at Q3 2026 while EBITDA rose from USD 123.7 million in FY2024 to USD 241.2 million on an LTM basis, so the improvement came from both repayment and earnings. The revolver was repaid to nil and the USD 550.0 million 2029 senior notes are now the only borrowings, which concentrates the creditor's refinancing exposure in one bullet maturity. Excluding the USD 32.6 million of tariff refunds booked in cost of goods sold, a normalisation that is Analyst Judgement and not a reported measure, net leverage would be 1.91x.

Capital expenditure is light at USD 14.5 million in FY2025, 0.77% of revenue, so cash generation depends on working capital and the inventory build ahead of the first-quarter and third-quarter peak shipping periods rather than on investment.

fields.value: The most material gap is that covenant levels, definitions and the reported covenant ratios are not printed, so the cushion between 1.66x net leverage and any maximum test cannot be stated and no covenant headroom is inferred. The call terms, security and ranking of the notes and the ranking of the revolver are also not stated, so the debt stack is not drawn. Interim interest cover and an adjusted EBITDA are the other missing items.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels, definitions, step-downs and the reported covenant ratios are not printed in any supplied filing, so covenant capacity and headroom cannot be stated for any period and none is inferred. Severity: High. Action: supply the credit agreement with its amendments or a compliance certificate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) is calculated as operating profit plus depreciation and amortization in every period, the adjusted rows and the adjusted EBITDA bridge are not written, and every leverage and cover ratio rests on a derived measure. Severity: Medium. Action: supply an issuer reconciliation or earnings release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is stated only in the annual report, so EBITDA over cash interest cannot be calculated for the LTM windows ending 2026-04-04, 2026-07-04 and 2026-10-03 and the interim cash flow columns carry no interest paid. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The call and redemption terms, the security and the ranking of the 4.000% senior notes, and the legal ranking of the Revolving Facility, are not stated in the filings, so the debt stack is not drawn and no secured or senior subtotal is stated. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the indenture and the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fiscal 2025 had 53 weeks and its fourth quarter had 14, so every LTM window ending in 2026 spans 53 weeks and is not like-for-like with a 52-week year. Severity: Medium. Action: state the 53-week basis beside every LTM figure.

fields.value: Wolverine World Wide Inc /De/ (issuer www-110471), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, transaction history and governance profile drawn from the five supplied SEC filings, for the latest period ended 2026-10-03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wolverine is a widely held public company with no sponsor or controlling holder in its filings, so owner extraction is not the main creditor risk; business concentration, tariff-exposed Asian sourcing and legacy environmental claims are, and governance risk is moderate. The Active Group supplies 75.1% of revenue and 71.4% of segment profit before corporate costs, while the Work Group is flat and losing margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder payouts are recurring but moderate against operating cash flow, debt has fallen by USD 100.6 million since the end of fiscal 2024, and no acquisition or new debt issue is described in the filings. The elimination of the Active Group president role in 2026 and the missing proxy statement and credit agreement leave board oversight and payout capacity unproven.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 87; calculation K10; calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No owner other than public shareholders is visible, so there is no sponsor to extract cash and none to supply a cure. The registrant is a Delaware corporation listed in New York with a few hundred holders of record, and no parent, fund or controlling shareholder is named in any of the five filings. The beneficial ownership table sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a large holder or activist cannot be ruled out, although a classified board with one-third of directors elected each year makes a sudden change of control harder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance disclosure is adequate for monitoring reported results but thin for creditor protection. The auditor gave unqualified opinions on the fiscal 2025 statements and on internal control, the Chairman of the Board is a separate person from the Chief Executive, and ten directors signed the annual report. Board independence, committees, compensation and related-party matters are in the proxy statement that is not supplied, and covenant levels are not printed. Executive turnover is visible: one of six executive officers listed in January 2025 was no longer listed a year later, a new Work Group president started in November 2025, and the Active Group president post was eliminated from the third quarter of 2026, with a separation agreement for the executive named in the annual report as its holder taking effect on 2026-10-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder payouts are recurring and moderate rather than extractive. Dividends of USD 33.3 million and repurchases of USD 14.5 million in fiscal 2025 equal 34.1% of operating cash flow of USD 140.0 million, while debt fell by USD 100.6 million between fiscal 2024 and the latest quarter and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-10-03. The repurchase came in November 2025, between revolver balances of USD 130.0 million at 2025-09-27 and USD 75.0 million at the year-end, USD 135.5 million of authorisation remains, and the covenants that limit dividends and buybacks are not supplied, so capacity for larger payouts is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The portfolio was pruned rather than levered. Disposals and sale-leasebacks in 2023 and 2024 raised USD 307.8 million, and the filing states the proceeds of the sales reduced revolver borrowings; no acquisition, divestiture or new debt issue is described in 2026. The one financing event is the September 2025 replacement of the revolver and term loan with a USD 600.0 million revolver due in 2030, whose aggregate debt capacity of up to USD 850.0 million leaves room for more debt that the filings do not show being used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings depend on the Active Group's performance brands, and the Work Group is the weaker segment. Active Group revenue grew by USD 161.7 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 112.8 million in the first nine months of 2026, led by Saucony and Merrell, while Work Group revenue was almost flat and its operating margin fell to 14.9% from 16.4%, with higher U.S. tariff costs cited for its lower gross margin. No customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but brand revenue levels are not printed, so the size of the Saucony and Merrell dependence is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 47–51; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36; calculation K6; calculation K7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sourcing is entirely outsourced to third-party suppliers, mainly in Asia Pacific, without long-term contracts, which keeps capital needs low but leaves margin exposed to tariffs. The USD 32.6 million refund of invalidated tariffs lifted third-quarter 2026 gross margin by 640 basis points and should be treated as one-off, and no asset is recognised for further claims. Capital expenditure is only 0.8% of revenue, so cash flow follows gross margin and working capital rather than investment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation K17; calculation K19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legacy environmental claims are a slow cash drain, not a near-term solvency risk. The remediation reserve is USD 21.4 million, of which USD 8.4 million is due within twelve months and the rest over up to 25 years; one landfill suit remains pending after a motion to dismiss was denied, and the company says it cannot estimate loss above reserves where remediation continues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Intangible assets are the main balance sheet risk to equity rather than to cash. Goodwill and intangibles of USD 633.8 million exceed total equity of USD 533.9 million, and the Sweaty Betty reporting unit passed its latest annual test by only 16% while its revenue fell by USD 6.1 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 3.5 million in the first nine months of 2026. An impairment would be non-cash, but whether it counts against the leverage and interest cover tests depends on definitions that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Part of working capital is funded off the balance sheet. Wholesale is 74.6% of revenue, and at 2026-10-03 the company had sold USD 125.0 million of receivables, the full facility limit, to purchasers through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary; those receivables are no longer company assets and the subsidiary's remaining assets are pledged to the purchasers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a moderate reading is conduct while debt was outstanding. The November 2025 repurchase and a dividend held at USD 0.10 per share each quarter were paid while revolver balances were outstanding at the quarter-ends reported, and the credit agreement and indenture that limit dividends and buybacks are not supplied, so payout capacity could be wide. Turnover in senior management when the Active Group carries most of the profit, a Work Group whose margin is falling and a pending environmental suit add to the case for a higher risk reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Against that, the filings print no related-party payments, no waiver, exchange offer or restructuring of any debt, a USD 100.6 million fall in debt since fiscal 2024, an undrawn revolver and unqualified audit opinions. A credit agreement with a wide restricted-payment basket, a large new holder or activist, a debt-funded acquisition or buyback, or a proxy statement showing related-party payments would move the view to higher risk. A proxy statement showing independent committees, together with tight payment limits in the credit agreement, would move it to lower risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Board independence, committee composition, compensation and related-party matters sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the moderate governance reading cannot be tightened to low and related-party leakage is not ruled out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Beneficial ownership is not supplied, so the finding that no controlling holder exists rests on the absence of any named sponsor or parent in the filings; a large holder would change the ownership and control reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so the capacity of the company to pay dividends, repurchase shares, add debt or move assets is not established; the moderate risk level rests on conduct, not on legal capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Brand revenue and profit are printed only as changes, so the dependence of the Active Group on Saucony and Merrell, and the share of Work Group revenue from the licensed Cat and Harley-Davidson brands, are stated by direction and not by size.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No document after the quarterly report signed on 2026-11-12 is supplied, so executive, ownership or financing changes since that date could change the governance reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction or new debt issue is described in the five filings for fiscal 2025 or 2026, and no transaction is pending. The portfolio changes in the filings are disposals and licensing in 2023 and 2024: the Keds, Sperry and leather businesses and the Hush Puppies rights in China, Hong Kong and Macau were sold, the Merrell and Saucony China joint ventures were sold to a licensee, and the kids and apparel lines of those two brands were licensed from May 2024, raising USD 307.8 million of cash with two sale-leasebacks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only financing event in the period is the 2025 Replacement Facility of 2025-09-24, which replaced the revolver and the term loan A with a USD 600.0 million revolver maturing 2030-09-24, guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries and secured on substantially all personal and real property, with aggregate debt capacity of up to USD 850.0 million including incremental debt. The USD 550.0 million 4.000% senior notes issued on 2021-08-26 are due 2029-08-15 and guaranteed by substantially all domestic subsidiaries; they are the only debt outstanding at 2026-10-03, when total debt was USD 547.4 million after USD 2.6 million of deferred financing costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A quarterly dividend of USD 0.10 per share was declared on 2026-11-02 for holders of record on 2027-01-04; it is a subsequent event after the 2026-10-03 balance sheet and is not in any period figure. The filings describe no refinancing plan, new issue or covenant amendment after the balance sheet date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by recurring shareholder payouts made while revolver balances were outstanding and by missing covenant, ownership and board evidence, because these leave the capacity for larger distributions and for related-party leakage untested, which implies limited protection for creditors beyond the observed debt reduction. Countervailing evidence is the USD 100.6 million fall in debt, the undrawn revolver, the absence of any waiver, exchange offer or restructuring and unqualified audit opinions. Further analysis requires the credit agreement, the indenture and the proxy statement.

fields.value: Wolverine World Wide Inc /De/ (issuer www-110471), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the fundamental credit synthesis drawn from the five supplied SEC filings and from the supplied Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs, for the latest period ended 2026-10-03.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wolverine's credit profile is adequate and improving, so near-term repayment risk is low, but it leans on Active Group brand momentum and a single bullet maturity in 2029. Net leverage fell to 1.66x of LTM EBITDA at Q3 2026 from 4.01x at FY2024, or 1.69x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-02, but USD 32.6 million of one-off tariff refunds flatter it: without the refunds it would be 1.91x before the dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation L3; calculation L4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 724.7 million against USD 550.0 million of senior notes due in 2029 gives a refinancing runway, and low capital spending keeps cash generation positive. The primary downside path is a fade in Active Group demand, or tariff costs without further refunds, eroding margin before the 2029 refinancing, with covenant headroom and the ranking of the notes not established because the credit agreement and indenture are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation L6; calculation L7; calculation L18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has moved from stretched to moderate through both repayment and earnings. Net debt to EBITDA was 4.01x at FY2024, 2.36x at FY2025 and 1.66x at Q3 2026, which is 1.69x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-02, with net debt falling from USD 495.9 million to USD 399.3 million (USD 407.5 million pro forma) while EBITDA rose from USD 123.7 million in FY2024 to USD 241.2 million on an LTM basis. That lowers debt service pressure and the weight of the 2029 maturity, but the ratio is seasonal: it was 2.76x at Q1 2026 after the first-quarter working capital build.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation L3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Part of the latest improvement is one-off, and the underlying margin is flat rather than rising. Tariff refunds of USD 32.6 million sit in cost of goods sold, so gross margin without them was 47.41% in the first nine months of 2026, level with 47.41% a year earlier, which means price increases and other gains only matched higher U.S. tariff costs and an unfavourable product and customer mix. EBITDA margin without the refund was 10.49% against 8.96% a year earlier because operating expenses grew 3.0% while revenue grew 8.3%, so operating leverage added 1.53 percentage points rather than the 3.75 percentage points reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation L11; calculation L12; calculation L13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2029 senior notes are the single refinancing event, and liquidity covers them with room to spare. Liquidity of USD 724.7 million, which is cash plus USD 576.6 million of unborrowed revolver, is 1.32x the USD 550.0 million principal, no debt matures before 2029-08-15 (about 33 months from the as-of date), and the notes carry an annual cash coupon of USD 22.0 million. The revolver ends 405 days after the notes, so it does not by itself bridge a failed refinancing, and whether it carries an earlier springing maturity is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L6; calculation L7; calculation L8; calculation L16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is positive but seasonal and driven by working capital, not investment. Capital expenditure was only USD 14.5 million in fiscal 2025, so free cash flow was USD 125.5 million, USD 77.7 million after USD 33.3 million of dividends and USD 14.5 million of repurchases, and USD 211.5 million on an LTM basis; nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 20.1 million in 2025 and positive USD 65.9 million in 2026. Revolver borrowings rose to USD 92.0 million at Q1 2026 from USD 75.0 million at the year-end before being repaid, so intra-year leverage and liquidity should be read against the same quarter a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation L9; calculation L10; calculation L24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business concentration is the main operating risk. The Active Group supplied 75.1% of fiscal 2025 revenue and 71.4% of segment profit before corporate costs, led by Saucony and Merrell, while the Work Group's operating margin fell to 14.9% from 16.4% in the first nine months of 2026; brand revenue levels are not printed, so the size of the dependence is not established, and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation L21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariffs and Asian sourcing are the main external risk, and no contract protects the margin. All products come from third-party suppliers, mainly in Asia Pacific, without long-term contracts, so U.S. tariff costs flow into cost of goods sold and are recovered only through price; the February 2026 court ruling produced a one-off refund and no further asset is recognised. Footwear is a competitive and fragmented market and wholesale customers order on an order-to-order basis, so the evidence of pricing power is price increases offsetting tariffs rather than margin expansion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside reported debt make obligations larger than the debt figure suggests. Total debt plus the USD 125.0 million of receivables sold is 2.79x LTM EBITDA, USD 137.3 million of lease liabilities and USD 53.0 million of accrued pension liabilities sit outside debt, and the USD 21.4 million environmental reserve will be paid over up to 25 years. Goodwill and intangibles of USD 633.8 million exceed equity of USD 533.9 million, so an impairment would hit equity but not cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 24–25; calculation L17; calculation L22; calculation L23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy and governance are moderate, and they hold the main unknowns for creditors. There is no sponsor, payouts are 38.1% of free cash flow and no waiver, exchange or restructuring is described, but the covenant levels, the security and ranking of the notes and the proxy statement are not available, so headroom and priority are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation L10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate and improving view is that the improvement is recent, flattered by a one-off and exposed to a seasonal cycle. Net leverage was 2.76x at Q1 2026, only two quarters before it reached 1.66x (1.69x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-02), EBITDA was negative USD 31.7 million in FY2023 and only USD 123.7 million in FY2024, nine-month free cash flow was negative in 2025, and at the FY2024 EBITDA level total debt to EBITDA would be 4.43x with the notes coupon covered 5.62x. Active Group concentration, a weakening Work Group and tariff exposure mean one weak season could reverse much of the gain, and no covenant levels are available to show how much room there would be.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation L3; calculation L18; calculation L27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Against that, debt is down USD 100.6 million since FY2024, no maturity falls before 2029, liquidity is 1.32x the notes, capital spending is light, and the income-statement interest burden is small at 9.07x LTM EBITDA to net interest expense. Evidence that would move the view weaker includes an Active Group revenue decline, EBITDA falling toward the FY2024 level, revolver borrowings above the USD 130.0 million seen in 2025, a buyback or dividend increase while it is drawn, or covenant terms that leave little room. Evidence that would move it stronger includes a refinancing of the 2029 notes at similar cost, covenant terms with wide headroom and a sustained Work Group margin recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation L7; calculation L15; calculation L24; calculation L28

fields.value: - The ranking and security of the senior notes are not stated, so how noteholders would rank against a fully drawn secured revolver of USD 600.0 million is not established; this bounds the refinancing conclusion and any view of recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging to a moderate level is the first strength. Repayment and EBITDA growth took net leverage from 4.01x to 1.66x, or 1.69x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-02, which lowers debt service pressure and the weight of the 2029 maturity and so lowers the probability of distress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L1; calculation L2; calculation L3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity against a single maturity is the second strength. Liquidity of USD 724.7 million covers the USD 550.0 million of notes due on 2029-08-15 by 1.32x and no other debt matures first, so a refinancing can be run without a liquidity squeeze if the revolver stays drawable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; calculation L6; calculation L7; calculation L16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset-light cash generation is the third strength. Capital expenditure of 0.8% of revenue means most EBITDA converts to free cash flow, which was USD 125.5 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 211.5 million over the LTM, supporting repayment and the dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation L9; calculation L10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Active Group brand momentum is the fourth strength. Active Group revenue rose USD 161.7 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 112.8 million in nine months of 2026, lifting EBITDA and the pace of repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation L21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration in the Active Group is the first weakness. The Active Group is 75.1% of revenue and 71.4% of segment profit, so a fade in Saucony or Merrell demand would reverse leverage gains quickly, and brand revenue levels are not printed to size the exposure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariff exposure and a flattered margin are the second weakness. Third-party Asian sourcing exposes cost of goods sold to tariffs, and USD 32.6 million of one-off refunds lift the latest margin, so leverage is 1.91x before the dividend without them and the underlying gross margin is flat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation L4; calculation L11; calculation L12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A single bullet maturity with unseen terms is the third weakness. All refinancing falls on 2029-08-15, a one percentage point higher coupon would cost USD 5.5 million a year, and covenant levels and the ranking of the notes are not available, so headroom and priority are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; calculation L16; calculation L19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside debt and intangibles above equity are the fourth weakness. Receivables sold, lease and pension liabilities and the remediation reserve sit outside the debt figure, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 633.8 million exceed equity of USD 533.9 million, so obligations are larger than debt and an impairment would weaken equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation L17; calculation L22; calculation L23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wolverine designs, markets and licenses casual, outdoor, athletic, work and kids' footwear and apparel through two reportable segments: the Active Group, with Merrell, Saucony, Sweaty Betty and Chaco, and the Work Group, with Wolverine, Cat, Bates, Harley-Davidson and HYTEST. Fiscal 2025 revenue was USD 1,874.3 million, 74.6% wholesale and 25.4% direct-to-consumer, with 52.2% earned outside the United States, and no customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue. Disposals and licensing deals in 2023 and 2024, including Keds, Sperry, leather and Hush Puppies in China and North America, cut Other revenue by 86.3%, leaving a brand-focused business with no owned factories.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 108

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wholesale orders are placed order by order and can be cancelled, so cash-flow visibility is short and rests on brand demand each season. The model needs little capital, which supports debt service in a normal year, but the main levers in a weak year are marketing spend and shareholder payouts rather than capital expenditure, so refinancing confidence depends on demand holding up until 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wolverine World Wide, Inc. is a widely held listed company with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named in any filing, so there is no owner to extract cash and none to cure a shortfall. The senior notes are guaranteed by substantially all domestic subsidiaries, and the USD 600.0 million revolver is guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries and secured on substantially all personal and real property; the security and ranking of the notes are not stated, so the noteholders' position against a drawn secured revolver is not established. Receivables are sold through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary whose assets are pledged to the purchasers, and noncontrolling interests of USD 20.2 million show that some subsidiaries are not wholly owned.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is moderate: dividends and repurchases took 38.1% of fiscal 2025 free cash flow, debt fell by USD 100.6 million since FY2024, and no waiver, exchange or restructuring is described, but the credit agreement that limits payouts is not supplied. Business & governance puts governance and sponsor risk at medium, driven by recurring payouts made while revolver balances were outstanding and by missing covenant, ownership and board evidence, which leaves capacity for larger distributions untested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation L10; calculation L28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue recovered after the disposals: USD 2,242.9 million in fiscal 2023, USD 1,755.0 million in fiscal 2024, USD 1,874.3 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 1,986.9 million on an LTM basis over 53 weeks. Growth is led by the Active Group, which added USD 161.7 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 112.8 million in nine months of 2026 on Saucony and Merrell, while the Work Group was flat and Hush Puppies royalty revenue declined. Nine-month 2026 growth of 8.3% includes a USD 17.7 million foreign exchange benefit and is 7.0% without it, and the filing cites price increases as a driver of gross margin, which shows some pricing power against tariffs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation L14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is discretionary and brand-driven, wholesale customers order on an order-to-order basis, retail consolidation and private label are named as risks, and only USD 23.8 million of fixed licence consideration gives contracted visibility. Revenue is therefore cyclical and moderately concentrated in the Active Group, so durability depends on Saucony and Merrell demand holding up and on direct-to-consumer, which grew 1.7% in nine months of 2026 after falling 1.7% in fiscal 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross margin rose to 47.3% in fiscal 2025 from 44.3% on cost savings, full-price mix and price increases, partly offset by higher U.S. tariffs. In the first nine months of 2026 reported gross margin was 49.63%, but without the USD 32.6 million tariff refund it was 47.41%, level with the prior year, so price increases and other gains only matched tariff costs and an unfavourable product and customer mix. Operating expenses were 39.3% of fiscal 2025 revenue and grew 3.0% against revenue growth of 8.3% in nine months of 2026, so operating leverage added 1.53 percentage points to EBITDA margin without the refund.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, pages 30–33; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation L11; calculation L12; calculation L13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through price and marketing spend, but a demand fall would meet operating expenses of USD 736.5 million that include store and lease costs the filing calls fixed, and there are no long-term supplier contracts to protect input costs. Margin resilience is therefore average: proven against tariffs only by price increases, and unproven through a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure was USD 14.5 million in fiscal 2025, 0.8% of revenue and 56.0% of depreciation and amortization, because manufacturing is outsourced. Free cash flow was USD 125.5 million in fiscal 2025, 71.27% of EBITDA, and USD 211.5 million on an LTM basis, but working capital swings it: operating cash flow was USD 73.6 million in nine months of 2026 against negative USD 6.2 million a year earlier, after a working capital outflow of USD 73.0 million.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest of USD 33.5 million in fiscal 2025 is already inside operating cash flow; dividends of USD 33.3 million and repurchases of USD 14.5 million leave USD 77.7 million. Further calls include remediation payments of USD 5.7 million in nine months of 2026, purchase obligations of USD 315.4 million due within a year for inventory and capital items, and operating lease obligations of USD 168.9 million. EBITDA converts to free cash flow reliably over a year but not within it, and capital expenditure offers little flexibility because it is already low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: the filing describes a competitive and fragmented market in which some rivals are larger and better resourced, so brand strength must be refreshed each season and margin depends on price, product and marketing. Buyer power is moderate: wholesale customers order on an order-to-order basis and retail consolidation and private label can squeeze terms, but no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and direct-to-consumer is a quarter of sales. Supplier power is low to moderate: all products are made by third parties without long-term contracts, but the filing says other suppliers could supply similar products on comparable terms, so switching is possible at some cost and delay. The supplied filings give no evidence on new entrants or substitutes, so those two forces are not assessed. Together the forces point to margin durability that rests on brand demand rather than structural protection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material. U.S. tariffs on imported goods feed cost of goods sold, the court ruling of 2026-02-20 produced USD 35.3 million of refunds by 2026-10-03, and a new tariff basis would remove that benefit; environmental law drives the USD 21.4 million remediation reserve. Economic factors matter through consumer demand and foreign exchange: forward contracts of USD 335.9 million hedge dollar inventory purchases of non-U.S. wholesale operations, and exchange rates added USD 17.7 million to nine-month revenue. The Middle East is about 1% of revenue and managed by distributors, so it is a minor exposure, and social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-supportive strengths are deleveraging to a moderate level, liquidity that covers the only maturity, asset-light cash generation, Active Group brand momentum and the absence of a sponsor. The credit constraints are concentration in the Active Group, a Work Group whose margin is falling, tariff exposure with a flattered latest margin, claims outside debt with intangibles above equity, and covenant and ranking terms that are not visible. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are an early refinancing of the 2029 notes, further debt reduction from cash flow and a Work Group margin recovery. Threats that could weaken it are new tariffs, a fade in Saucony and Merrell demand, an impairment of the Sweaty Betty reporting unit and larger shareholder payouts while the revolver is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: LTM revenue of USD 1,986.9 million across recognised brands in a fragmented market. Competitive advantage is average: brand names and licences support pricing, but the Cat and Harley-Davidson licences end in 2028 and 2029 and price increases only offset tariffs. Business diversification is average: two segments, 52.2% foreign revenue and no customer above 10%, but 75.1% of revenue sits in the Active Group. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital expenditure is low, but operating expenses are 39.3% of revenue. Margin stability is average and improving but unproven through a cycle. Free cash flow stability is average: positive in every full fiscal year from 2023 to 2025 but negative over nine months of 2025. Ability to refinance is average on the evidence available, because the bullet is about 33 months away and no rating or market price is supplied. Liquidity position is strong because USD 724.7 million of liquidity faces no maturity before 2029. Financial policy and governance are average: no sponsor and moderate payouts, with covenants not visible. The trend is improving.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the supports are Active Group momentum, with Active Group revenue up 9.9% in the third quarter of 2026, lower interest cost as debt was repaid, price increases and operating cash flow that the company expects to be sufficient for working capital. The headwinds are U.S. tariff costs without the 2026 refund, a Work Group whose margin is 1.5 percentage points lower, rising advertising and selling costs, a 53-week base in the LTM measures and continuing remediation payments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the Cat licence ends in 2028 and the Harley-Davidson licence in 2029, the notes mature in 2029 and the revolver in 2030, so licence renewals and refinancing fall in the same window. No management guidance is supplied, so this outlook rests on reported trends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with a fade in Active Group demand for Saucony and Merrell combined with U.S. tariffs on Asian-sourced goods continuing without further refunds. Wholesale customers that order on an order-to-order basis cut or cancel orders and markdowns rise, so revenue and gross margin fall while inventory of USD 278.2 million builds and the full-price mix that helped fiscal 2025 reverses. EBITDA then falls toward the USD 123.7 million of FY2024, 48.7% below the LTM level, which would put total debt to EBITDA at 4.43x while the USD 22.0 million notes coupon is still covered 5.62x. The seasonal working capital build is financed on the revolver, which reached USD 130.0 million in 2025 and still left USD 456.0 million unborrowed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-10-03_www-20261003.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation L3; calculation L8; calculation L18; calculation L24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2029 notes would then be refinanced into a weaker market, and each percentage point on the coupon costs USD 5.5 million a year. The management levers are dividends and repurchases of USD 47.8 million, marketing spend, inventory and store closures, while capital expenditure is too small to cut and the 2023 and 2024 disposals show asset sales can raise cash. On these figures resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress before 2029, so default is not supported by the evidence; the exposure is refinancing cost and covenant room, which is not established. Observable triggers are Active Group revenue turning negative, gross margin without refunds below 47.41%, revolver borrowings above USD 130.0 million and any buyback while it is drawn.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-K_2026-01-03_www-20260103.htm.jsonl, page 110; calculation L10; calculation L19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Wolverine presents an adequate business profile supported by Active Group brand momentum, asset-light cash generation and a single bond with an undrawn revolver, but credit quality is constrained by concentration in the Active Group, tariff exposure with a flattered latest margin, claims outside debt and covenant and ranking terms that are not visible. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow was positive in every full fiscal year and USD 211.5 million over the LTM, although it is seasonal and working-capital driven. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Active Group results through 2028, covenant terms, the ranking of the notes and the rate environment, with USD 724.7 million of liquidity against USD 550.0 million of notes as the cushion. The primary downside path is a fade in Active Group demand or tariff costs without refunds eroding margin before the 2029 refinancing. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indenture, brand-level revenue and management guidance. Top risk: refinancing the 2029 notes after a margin setback.
